{{Quote|His armada dwindling, Xim sought to protect his battleships in the same manner of his war-robots. Employing techniques the Hutts had yet to master, his shipwrights forged dreadnaught hulls speckled with a special ore called kiirium that would reflect laser beams. But the ore was a most precious supply at the time, since the Kiirium Reaches had been mined and exhausted of their namesake.|[[Professor/Legends|Professor]] [[S. V. Skynx/Legends|S. V. Skynx]], ''[[The Despotica Reader]]'', [[The Despotica Reader, Third Edition|Third Edition]]|<ref name="Despotica">{{Hyperspace|url=fans/hyperspace/source/ximweek02/index.html|text=Xim Week: ''The Despotica'' (Part I)|int=Xim Week: The Despotica}}</ref>}}
The '''Ash Worlds''', a region that was originally known as the '''Kiirium Reaches''', was a [[Sector/Legends|sector]] located in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]].

==History==
===Settlement===
The Kiirium Reaches were settled by [[Human/Legends|Humans]] in ages before the rise of [[Xer VIII]] in the Tion Cluster. [[Xim/Legends|Xim the Despot]] quickly expanded his [[Xim's empire|empire]] into these worlds between [[25,120 BBY|25,120]] and [[25,096 BBY]]. The region was dubbed the Kiirium Reaches, and the lush planets [[Wyndigal 2|Huronom]] and [[OHS3842-03|Astigone]] became the Seventh and Eighth Thrones of the empire.<ref name="Xim Week" />

===Destruction===
After the defeat of Xim, the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]] made the Kiirium Reaches a buffer between the [[Hutt Empire]] and the Tion Cluster, regularly raiding it for slaves. After the [[Tionese (group)/Legends|Tionese]] made contact with the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] in [[24,500 BBY]], however, the Hutts saw this as the prelude to an alliance against them. Taking pre-emptive action, the Hutts exterminated the [[Tionese (group)/Legends|Tionese]] to the last man, woman, and child within the old borders of the Kiirium Reaches in a genocidal campaign known as [[the Devouring]]. Their settlements were vaporized, their worlds bombarded and poisoned, their histories, and eventually even their names erased.<ref name="Xim Week" /> The planets' names were lost and most were renamed.<ref name="TEA" /> Xim's [[Hyperspace beacon/Legends|hyperspace beacons]] were destroyed or towed away for the Hutts' own purposes, leaving future [[Scout/Legends|explorers]] to find new [[Hyperspace route/Legends|routes]] through the desolation. Only the beacons and a few Tionese worlds along the [[Salin Corridor/Legends|Salin Corridor]] (known at this time as Warriors' Trace) were spared to preserve a potential Hutt invasion corridor to the Tion and make sure there were hostages to take along the way. The location of the historical Kiirium Reaches was lost and was the subject of much debate among scholars for millennia. The locations of Huronom and Astigone were forgotten, and they became known as the Lost Thrones of Xim. [[Columex/Legends|Columex]] and [[Trogan/Legends|Trogan]] were popular suggestions for the location of Huronom, and numerous luxury resorts on [[Centares/Legends|Centares]] bore the name Astigone to claim the title of the Eighth Throne. Farther afield, the likes of [[Jabiim/Legends|Jabiim]], [[Lucazec/Legends|Lucazec]] and even [[Lantillies/Legends|Lantillies]] were proposed as Lost Thrones.<ref name="Xim Week" />

This region of thousands of barren worlds still bearing the invisible scars of radiation was finally called the Ash Worlds, a name so widely known that the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] adopted it for that [[Sector/Legends|sector]] of space.<ref name="Xim Week" /> The spared Kiirium [[Star system/Legends|star systems]] along the Salin Corridor were not included in the Ash Worlds.<ref name="EAOC" /> [[Astronomer/Legends|Astronomers]] had scoured the area searching for the remnants of a [[Supernova/Legends|supernova]] or some other devastating natural event, but nothing had ever been found.<ref name="Xim Week" />

The Devouring was remembered in a garbled fashion on many worlds of the [[Tion Cluster/Legends|Tion Cluster]] as a winter holiday. For some worlds such as [[Stalimur]], the holiday was a time for pious reflection, and the day even took the name "the Devouring". On other worlds it was a more light-hearted festival, such as the [[Wakemeet]] of [[Barseg]].<ref name="Xim Week" />

===Rediscovery===
After [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] interdicted many of the Ash Worlds for weapons research. However, this did not discourage the [[Historian/Legends|historian]] [[Bleys Harand]], who made numerous secret expeditions into the Ash Worlds. Harand and his students, including his protégé [[Henrietya Antilles]], explored the Ash Worlds and reported that the radiation levels on numerous planets fit the profile of [[fission bomb]] attacks some twenty-five thousand years earlier. With the [[Hutt Empire]] known to have conducted similar actions, Harand argued that the Ash Worlds were a remnant of the Kiirium Reaches, and that the Devouring holiday was a memory of a genocidal campaign waged by the Hutts against the Tionese.<ref name="Xim Week" />

Further explorations into the [[Tion Cluster/Legends|Tion Cluster]] led to Henrietya Antilles' discovery of the [[Great Duinarbulon Mausoleum]], which contained a large number of ancient records. After deciphering one of them, the [[Antilles Map]], Harand was proved correct: the Map showed that the hostile world of [[Wyndigal 2]] was once Huronom, while the anonymous [[OHS3842-03]] had been Astigone.<ref name="Xim Week" />

Harand's theory about the Kiirium Reaches was quickly accepted by [[Ximology|Ximologists]] and by [[30 ABY/Legends|30 ABY]] was considered the academic consensus.<ref name="Xim Week" />
